issues.description: Class field identifiers in the solution's Lecture.java are declared with snake_case names (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor and other members refer to camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) as specified by the UML in the problem statement. Specifically, the solution declares snake_case fields (solution Lecture.java lines 6-10) while the constructor signature and body use camelCase parameters and assign to this.lectureName etc. (solution Lecture.java line 13 and following). This mismatch will cause compilation errors (e.g., "cannot find symbol: variable lectureName") and directly confuses students about which field names they are expected to implement according to the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field identifiers in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java consistent with the UML and the rest of the class. Rename the declared fields from snake_case to camelCase: lecture_name -> lectureName, number_of_inscribed_students -> numberOfInscribedStudents, number_of_guest_students -> numberOfGuestStudents, number_of_lecturers -> numberOfLecturers, number_of_tutors -> numberOfTutors. Ensure constructor assignments, getters, setters and toString() reference these same camelCase fields so the class compiles and matches the problem specification.
